fixes.explanation: Not quite, baker. The song says these are “…plans formed long ago…” That's the timing the song gives. I've thrown a batch together in a hurry before, but the song has something much older in mind.

Close to the right idea, but the timing is off by a lot. The song says “…plans formed long ago…” and that's much older than last year. The song also says God worked them out in perfect faithfulness. My cookies don't last that long, and I stamp them for a living.

That's it, baker. The song says, “Therefore, a strong people will honor You.” It goes on to say the cities of ruthless nations will revere Him. Strong people and ruthless nations both show up in that verse.
That's not what the song says, baker. It says a strong people will honor God, and the cities of ruthless nations will revere Him (Isaiah 25:3). Hiding isn't anywhere in that verse.

The song doesn't name them here, baker. It says God has been “…a refuge for the poor, a stronghold for the needy in distress…” I might have guessed a fancier list, but the song keeps it to the poor and the needy. I think that says something about where the shelter goes.

Not quite, baker. Isaiah says the LORD of Hosts will prepare a lavish banquet “…for all the peoples…” Seating one group at that table would be like packing one cookie in a giant box. This banquet is a lot bigger than that.
Not the sea, baker. Isaiah says, “He will swallow up death forever.” The sea doesn't show up in that line. Death is what gets swallowed up.
Not this one, baker. Isaiah says, “He will swallow up death forever.” That word is forever, not a little while. So the answer is False.
Close, but that's not the word. They say, “we have waited for Him, and He has saved us.” Then they say, “This is the LORD for whom we have waited.” So waiting is the word, not searching.

That's not what they say, baker. They say, “we have waited for Him, and He has saved us.” No hammers in that verse. They also say, “Let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation.” Waiting is what they say they've been doing.
That's it, trampled. Isaiah says, “…Moab will be trampled in his place…” The verse is blunt, and it's heavy.
No crown here, baker. Isaiah says, “…Moab will be trampled in his place…” That's a hard line, and it's the opposite of a crown.
Not hidden, baker. Isaiah says, “…Moab will be trampled in his place…” No hiding spot in this verse, and it's a heavy one.
